text.en: Asha moved a magnet near a coil connected to a small bulb and the bulb glowed for a moment. "Magnetism made electricity!" she cried.

The region around a magnet where its influence is felt is the magnetic field. A magnetic field line points along the field at every point. Magnetic flux measures the field passing through a surface. It depends on field strength, area and orientation. A current-carrying wire also produces a magnetic field around it, which is the magnetic effect of current.
A current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field can feel a force when the current crosses the field. Fleming’s left-hand rule gives the force direction. This force is used in the electric motor, which changes electrical energy into mechanical energy.
A change in magnetic flux through a coil induces a voltage. When the conducting path is closed, this voltage can drive a current. This is electromagnetic induction, and Lenz's law says the induced current flows so as to oppose the change that causes it. The electric generator uses it to change mechanical energy into electrical energy.
A transformer changes alternating voltage. A step-up transformer changes a low voltage to a high voltage and a step-down transformer changes a high voltage to a low voltage. Transformers work only with alternating current.

Put a compass at several positions around a bar magnet in a classroom diagram. The compass points in the local field direction. At a new position, the arrow may turn.

board.text: Compass direction samples the local field

text.en: Outside a bar magnet, field lines point from north toward south. Inside the magnet, the lines close the loop. They do not cross, because the field at a given point has one direction.

board.text: Outside: N → S; field lines form loops

text.en: A diagram can use closer lines in places where the field is stronger. The lines are a drawing convention used to describe the field.

board.text: Closer lines represent a stronger field

text.en: Turn a flat loop in a steady magnetic field. Flux is greatest in magnitude when the field passes straight through the opening, and zero when the field runs parallel to the plane of the loop.
Oersted observed that current in a nearby wire made a compass turn. The compass provided evidence that electric current creates a magnetic field.
Around a long straight wire, field direction follows circles centred on the wire. With the right thumb pointing along conventional current, curled fingers show the field direction.
Reverse the current in the same wire. Its magnetic field direction reverses too. The rule uses conventional current direction.
A coil combines magnetic fields from its turns. A long coil, called a solenoid, can create a fairly uniform field inside. An iron core can strengthen the field in a classroom electromagnet.

board.text: Coil + suitable core → stronger magnetic effect

text.en: In the motor effect, current crossing an external field can give a sideways force. If current and field are parallel, the ideal straight wire has no magnetic force from that field.

board.text: Crossing current and field can produce force

text.en: Use Fleming’s left-hand rule to keep the directions separate. The first finger shows field, the middle finger shows conventional current and the thumb shows the force.
Parallel wires carrying current in the same direction attract. When their directions are opposite, the wires repel. Each wire produces a field that pushes or pulls on the other wire’s current.

board.text: Parallel currents: same way attract, opposite ways repel

text.en: On opposite sides of a motor coil, the current runs in opposite directions. In the same external field, the forces act in opposite directions and can turn the coil.

board.text: Opposite forces create a turning effect

text.en: In a simple direct-current motor, a split-ring commutator reverses the coil current at the appropriate points. The coil can then keep turning in the same rotary direction.
Now move a bar magnet toward a stationary coil in a diagram. The field passing through the coil changes, and the indicator can deflect while that change occurs.
Hold the magnet still. The coil can remain in a magnetic field while the flux stays constant. The induction signal disappears once the motion and change stop.

board.text: Steady flux → no induced voltage in this example

text.en: Pull the magnet away instead. The change of flux reverses, so the induced current also reverses in the simple closed-coil circuit. Its field opposes the change that produced it.

board.text: Reverse the change → reverse induced current

text.en: A second coil can also experience changing flux when the current in a nearby coil changes. If the first current settles at a steady value, the second coil no longer has an induction signal from that change.

board.text: Changing current in one coil can affect another

text.en: In a simple generator, a coil turns in a magnetic field. The changing flux produces a voltage. A turning source such as a turbine provides the input energy.
Fleming’s right-hand rule is used in the simple generator diagram. The thumb shows conductor motion, the first finger shows field and the middle finger shows induced conventional current.

board.text: Right hand: motion · field · induced current

text.en: A transformer uses a changing field in one coil to induce voltage in another. In the ideal model, more turns on the secondary than the primary give a larger secondary voltage.
If a pictured transformer has one hundred primary turns and fifty secondary turns, its ideal secondary voltage is half the primary voltage. The diagram shows a step-down transformer.
Compare the three devices. A motor uses current to produce motion. A generator uses motion to produce a voltage. A transformer changes voltage by linking coils with a changing magnetic field.

problem.en: An ideal transformer has 100 primary turns, 50 secondary turns and 12 V AC across the primary. Find the secondary voltage.

text.en: Divide the secondary turns by the primary turns.

why.en: Fifty divided by one hundred gives one half.

text.en: Multiply the twelve volt primary reading by one half.

why.en: The output in the ideal model is six volts, so this is a step-down transformer.

prompt.en: A friend says A magnet and a coil must always be moving apart to give current. How will you reply?

requiredIdeas.en: Any change in magnetic flux through the coil induces an emf.
Moving towards or away both work.

points.en: A motor turns electrical energy into motion.
Transformers step voltage up or down.
